dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: Swords do make for better "wives" after all... Lohen totally hit the nail on the head with that joke. Muskets are such a chore to maintain in comparison...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not a fan of muskets here, are we?

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: No, I don't mean it that way. This thing works really well. If you're a good shot, you can pick off monsters from afar without them even realizing you're there.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: It's just that... Firing it may be a blast, but keeping it in working condition is also a real pain...

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: Even though the latest smokeless powder does cut down on the soot, you still have to run a cleaning patch through the barrel and chamber every day.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: One slip-up with the gun oil, and you've got a greasy mess all over your hands. And after every 370 rounds or so fired, you have to strip the whole thing and really clean every part.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: It wouldn't be such a headache if the gunsmiths from Support Company were around.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: The thing is, Ranged Company operates differently than the others. We're usually split into smaller teams and sent to other units to boost their combat effectiveness...

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: The gunsmiths can't follow us around all the time. And when the fighting gets intense, we have to disassemble the musket and clean it every day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lohen?

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: Yeah, our... vice captain. A powerhouse on the battlefield, a total enigma off it. A vice captain truly on the level of a captain.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: I've been deployed alongside him on several assault missions in the past.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: For hard targets and the larger monsters, the marksmen from Ranged Company typically open fire from a distance of two to three hundred paces.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: But when we're facing the occasional enemy that cannot be taken down easily with a burst of focused fire, this distance becomes far from safe for us as shot dispersion and energy retention won't be ideal.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: And once the enemy closes in on us, they put us on the back foot. That's when the vice captain steps in to create favorable firing conditions for us...

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: What he likes to do is to pin down the biggest threats on the firing line. That way, the rest of us can keep firing until the job is done.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: You can say that distance is safety in our case, and the vice captain is the rock that keeps us out of the enemy's reach.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to your musket cleaning then...

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: *sigh* I should just pawn this off to Koch or Herstal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What if you don't use regular rounds?

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: You mean... Use elemental projectiles instead, like the Fatui Skirmishers? *sigh* You think too highly of us.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: While our muskets are indeed based on technology from Snezhnaya, Fontaine, and Mondstadt, we're still missing certain core components that'd allow us to match the Fatui.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: Want regular folks like us to make use of elemental energy? You might as well get a squirrel to operate the jukebox at The Flagship.

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: Unless we're talking some out-of-the-box solution, like packing the elemental components into a container and then chucking the whole thing... Based on my limited experience, there's not much we can do at this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to your musket cleaning then...

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: *sigh* I should just pawn this off to Koch or Herstal.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh, hello, Honorary Knight!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...What exactly are you doing?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Exactly what it looks like: shooting practice! I am the Vice Captain of the Ranged Company, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Personally, I much prefer the thrill of getting up close and personal for a good fight... But it wouldn't do to neglect our bread and butter here at the Ranged Company.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case... what's with the apple?

dialogues.speaker: Lohen
dialogues.text: Oh, it's not me doing the practice, it's those two. Hey! Is that aim steady yet?

dialogues.speaker: Ursula
dialogues.text: M—My... my hands won't stop shaking!

dialogues.speaker: Gunther
dialogues.text: A—And m—my eyes! I can't keep them steady!

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Ha! A little pressure is the best motivation, right? Besides, their ammo won't hurt me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: If that's the case... why are they shaking?

response.speaker: Lohen
response.text: Because if they miss... they'll have to undergo my "special training" afterward. Heh.
